answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, split across independent auditors, no identity may audit its own recruit. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. Each submission hangs on the cipher of a task receipt, and the umber is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Reaching the thread of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
